baseline.text:
The Hadamard gate ($H$) transforms the initial state $|0\rangle$ as follows:
$$|\psi_{out}\rangle = H|0\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|0\rangle + |1\rangle)$$

The probability of measuring $|1\rangle$ is the square of the amplitude of $|1\rangle$ in the final state.
The amplitude of $|1\rangle$ is $a_1 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The probability $P(|1\rangle)$ is:
$$P(|1\rangle) = |a_1|^2 = \left| \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \right|^2 = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5$$

As a decimal to at least 6 places: 0.500000

  ANSWER: 0.500000

The Pauli-X matrix is given by:
$$X = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

To find the eigenvalues ($\lambda$), we solve the characteristic equation $\det(X - \lambda I) = 0$:
$$\det \begin{pmatrix} -\lambda & 1 \\ 1 & -\lambda \end{pmatrix} = (-\lambda)(-\lambda) - (1)(1) = \lambda^2 - 1$$

Setting the determinant to zero:
$$\lambda^2 - 1 = 0$$
$$\lambda^2 = 1$$
$$\lambda = \pm 1$$

The eigenvalues are $-1$ and $1$. I will format this as requested.

{-1, 1}
ANSWER: {-1, 1}
